source: Safe because the poll takes any Submitted order older than the grace period and "OrderDate" is unchanged (OrderProcessor/Services/GracePeriodOrdersRepository.cs:24-28); each setter acts only from its expected state, so a late original answer is ignored (Ordering.Domain/AggregatesModel/OrderAggregate/Order.cs:101, 110, 121); the stock check reserves nothing (Catalog.API/IntegrationEvents/EventHandling/OrderStatusChangedToPaidIntegrationEventHandler.cs:12; Catalog.API/IntegrationEvents/EventHandling/OrderStatusChangedToAwaitingValidationIntegrationEventHandler.cs:15-25); payment is the stateless simulated setting (PaymentProcessor/IntegrationEvents/EventHandling/OrderStatusChangedToStockConfirmedIntegrationEventHandler.cs:21-28). A late payment-failed answer still cancels the order (Ordering.Domain/AggregatesModel/OrderAggregate/Order.cs:142-153), which matches its result. With a real payment gateway in its place, sending a StockConfirmed order round again could take payment twice

action: Do not set "OrderStatus" straight to 'StockConfirmed', 'Paid' or 'Cancelled' by SQL: the events are raised only inside the setters, so no outbox row is written and nothing after it happens (payment, stock reduction, notifications)
Do not set an outbox row's "State" back to 0 to have it sent: nothing reads unsent rows after the request that wrote them
Do not look for failed messages to replay: a consumer acknowledges a message it failed on, and no dead-letter queue exists
Do not restart order-processor to move orders held in AwaitingValidation or StockConfirmed: the poll selects only Submitted
Do not restart the postgres or eventbus container apps as a first move: no data volume is declared for either, so find out where their data lives first
